article_title: Paramount's $110 Billion Warner Bros. Discovery Deal Clears US Antitrust Review but Now Hinges on a July 22 EU Deadline and UK Scrutiny
summary: Accurate, neutrally framed M&A/antitrust story; all quotes and specifics verified against source snapshots (CBS via last-resort WebFetch after its snapshot 406'd). One recoverable date imprecision filed as a correction. The automated REJECT stemmed from a CBS bot-block (406) and off-allowlist outlets, both resolved editorially.

content_preview.title: Paramount's $110 Billion Warner Bros. Discovery Deal Clears US Antitrust Review but Now Hinges on a July 22 EU Deadline and UK Scrutiny
content_preview.summary: The Justice Department cleared Paramount's $110 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery without conditions, over reported objections from career antitrust staff, leaving an EU remedy decision due July 22 and possible UK intervention as the deal's final hurdles.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The U.S. Justice Department's Antitrust Division cleared Paramount Skydance's roughly $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on Friday, June 12, 2026, without requiring any divestitures or conditions, [according to CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/paramount-skydance-warner-bros-discovery-antitrust-justice-department/). In its statement the department said the transaction "is not likely to result in harm to competition or American consumers," [as reported by CBS New...

recommendations: Prefer at least one allowlisted wire/newspaper source for the DOJ-clearance lede where available; thewrap.com, commondreams.org and screendaily.com are off-allowlist but were substantively corroborated against each other and CBS.
When attributing a report to a date, use the wire's actual publication date (WSJ Monday June 15) rather than the aggregator's date (Common Dreams June 16).

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (638 words). Overview/What We Know/What We Don't Know format is clear. Correctly separates verified US clearance from the pending EU (July 22) and possible UK steps, and flags open state-AG exposure. Headline and summary are accurate and appropriately hedged ('possible UK intervention', 'final hurdles').
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all four source snapshots. source-1.html.gz (TheWrap, June 15 2026, HTTP 200): CONFIRMS the $110B figure, the 'eight months... leaning towards recommending a lawsuit to challenge the merger' quote, 'senior DOJ officials... signed off... before they could make a final recommendation', Woodward's verbatim rebuttal 'A team of career lawyers never reached out to anyone in their leadership chain of command to express this, but instead reached out to you?', Paramount's verbatim 'pro-competitive, resulting in a stronger company better positioned to compete...', and Bonta's 'not a done deal and remains under investigation'. source-2.html.gz (Common Dreams, datePublished 2026-06-16, HTTP 200): CONFIRMS the career-lawyers quote 'leaning toward recommending a lawsuit challenging it on the grounds that the combination of the two movie studios would be anticompetitive and violate antitrust law', 'didn't participate in writing' the DOJ statement, Warren's verbatim 'The American people need to know if this merger was approved as a political favor' / 'This reeks of corruption', and Ellison dining with the president in April 2026; the piece attributes the underlying report to WSJ 'on Monday' (June 15), NOT June 16. source-3.html.gz (Screen Daily, July 1 2026, HTTP 200): CONFIRMS $110bn, commitments submitted June 30, EU deadline extended to July 22 from July 7, Paramount's verbatim remedy statement, the UIP/Universal joint-venture divestiture, the UK's June 30 possible-intervention statement 'because of the potential impact on news, children's television and streaming services', and Australia/Austria/Kuwait approvals. CBS News snapshot FAILED (HTTP 406 bot-block, file: null); per policy I fell back to WebFetch of the live URL, which CONFIRMS all four CBS-attributed specifics: the June 12 2026 clearance date, the DOJ 'not likely to result in harm to competition or American consumers' statement, Paramount's 'pro-competitive' quote, and Bonta's 'The merger of Warner Bros and Paramount is not a done deal and remains under investigation'.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All quotes verbatim (partial quotes are honest truncations of full source quotes). Deal value 'roughly $110 billion' is well supported (TheWrap/Screen Daily/CBS say $110B; Common Dreams says $111B, so 'roughly' is appropriate). One imprecision: the article calls the internal-dissent report 'the Journal's June 16 reporting', but both snapshots show the WSJ reported 'on Monday' (June 15); June 16 is Common Dreams' own publication date. Filed as a correction.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. Loaded quotes (Warren 'reeks of corruption') are clearly attributed to their speakers, and the DOJ/Woodward rebuttal is given equal footing. No editorializing or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Original. The only recent Paramount article (2026-06/13) covers a games-studio reorg, an unrelated topic. No prior coverage of the antitrust/merger-approval story.
concerns: Three of four sources (thewrap.com, commondreams.org, screendaily.com) are off the source allowlist. Judged acceptable editorially: they corroborate one another and CBS, and the underlying facts (WSJ dissent report, EU remedy filing) are cross-confirmed. Allowlist not modified.
CBS snapshot 406'd (bot-block, not a genuine dead link). Verified via last-resort live WebFetch as permitted when a snapshot fails.
recommendations: Attribute report dates to the originating wire's publication date, not the aggregator's.
editor_notes.corrections_filed: One correction: the phrase 'the Journal's June 16 reporting' — the WSJ reported on Monday June 15 (per both TheWrap and Common Dreams); June 16 is Common Dreams' publication date.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, well-sourced, and correctly framed (US cleared without conditions; EU/UK/state-AG steps still pending). Every specific traces to a cited source. The single date imprecision is minor, sits in a subordinate clause, and is honestly summarizable in a corrections note, so APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS rather than REJECT.
